title: Remove repeated attempts and check the timestamps
prompt:
The export was re-run once, so some attempts appear twice, and a few rows can't be placed in time. Every report is measured as of one fixed day, `AS_OF_DATE`: the last day of the data, 2026-06-28. It is a constant in the file, never today's date, so the numbers come out the same whenever the pipeline runs.

Write `clean_attempts(attempts)`. It starts from your `attempt_view(attempts)`, removes the copies and keeps only attempts that happened by the as-of date.
rules: A copy is an exact repeat: every column the same. Keep one of them.
An attempt with no `started_at` can't be placed in time: drop it.
Keep attempts whose `activity_date` is on or before `AS_OF_DATE`. One started at 23:15 on 2026-06-28 stays; one on 2026-06-29 is dropped.
An abandoned attempt (no `score_pct`, `passed` false) is real activity: it stays.
hints: Call `attempt_view(attempts)` first. `dropDuplicates()` with no columns removes exact copies.
Compare the day, not the timestamp: `F.col("activity_date") <= AS_OF_DATE`. A timestamp compared with "2026-06-28" means midnight, so it would drop that whole day.
A missing date fails any comparison, but saying `F.col("started_at").isNotNull()` makes the rule plain.
explanation: `dropDuplicates()` on the view removes rows that repeat in every column, which is exactly what a re-run export produces, so one attempt can't count twice in any later report. Filtering on `activity_date` rather than `started_at` keeps the whole as-of day: comparing a timestamp with the string "2026-06-28" compares with midnight and would lose that day's activity. Rows with no start time are dropped because no report can say when they happened. Abandoned attempts stay: they never pass a lesson, but they show a learner was there.
